name: gsm7_ascii_hello
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). Encoding is 'utf-8', not 'gsm0338': decoder.py calls gsm0338.decode(), which does not exist in the gsm0338 package (1.1.0 exports only Codec and find_gsm0338), so the AttributeError is swallowed by a bare except and every GSM-7 decode falls through to auto-detection. Harmless for plain ASCII, wrong for any body using GSM positions 0x00 (@), 0x02 ($), 0x11 (_), 0x24, 0x40 or 0x5B-0x7F.

name: auto_iso88595_privet
note: Expected mojibake, documented in the Python suite: without a DCS hint, short ISO-8859-5 and CP1251 bytes are indistinguishable and CP1251 is tried first. Use DCS 0x06 (dcs6_iso88595_berite) when the exact codec matters.

name: baidu_mixed_gb_utf16_auto
note: The production 'Baidu' message: a GB-encoded prefix followed by UTF-16BE. Auto-detection counts more odd-position nulls than even and picks utf-16-le, framing it one byte off. Kept because it is the message the Python suite was written around; baidu_mixed_gb_utf16_dcs8 shows what the correct DCS produces.

name: dcs6_cp1251_berite_tovary
note: CP1251 sent under DCS 0x06, the common real-world mismatch: both candidates score 13, and the tie goes to whichever was tried first, which is why CP1251 leads the list.

name: dcs14_euckr_annyeong
note: x/text's korean.EUCKR is windows-949, a superset of EUC-KR; identical for this body but it will accept a few sequences CPython's euc_kr rejects.

name: dcs240_msgclass_gsm7_test
note: DCS 0xF0 resolves to GSM-7 and then falls through to auto-detection; see gsm7_ascii_hello.

name: dcs244_msgclass_binary
note: DCS 0xF4 resolves through the message-class group to binary.

name: dcs192_msgwaiting_gsm7
note: DCS 0xC0 resolves to GSM-7 and then falls through to auto-detection; see gsm7_ascii_hello.

name: dcs5_shiftjis_konnichiwa
note: x/text's japanese.ShiftJIS follows the WHATWG index; identical for this body.

name: dcs13_eucjp_konnichiwa
note: DCS 0x0D tries EUC-JP before Shift-JIS.

name: auto_iso88595_privet_upper
note: Same as auto_iso88595_privet; the Python test asserts only that Cyrillic came out, not which word.

name: auto_latin1_french
note: KNOWN FAILING: reaches step 5, charset_normalizer, which picks cp1250 and corrupts 'Voilà' to 'Voilŕ'. Go has no charset_normalizer 2.0.4 equivalent and this package deliberately implements no substitute detector. The Go answer is ('Voil caf rsum', 'utf-8-lossy') — what Python itself returns when charset_normalizer is not installed. Both are mojibake; neither is the correct 'Voilà café résumé'. Python's own test only asserts "'café' in text or 'Voilà' in text", which passes on the corrupted string.

name: udh_concat_gsm7_hello_world
note: UDH stripped, then DCS 0x00 routed to auto-detection; see gsm7_ascii_hello.

name: false_udh_not_stripped
expected_text: Hello World, this is a longer message that is definitely not UDH
note: First byte is 0x05 but the IE chain does not validate, so ParseUDH refuses and the body is left whole. A naive length-byte heuristic would eat the first six characters.

name: no_udh_first_byte_high
note: KNOWN FAILING: b'\x80Hello' reaches charset_normalizer, which picks cp437 and yields 'ÇHello'. The Go answer is ('Hello', 'utf-8-lossy'), which is Python's own answer without charset_normalizer installed.

name: truncated_udh_ie
note: ParseUDH rejects the truncated IE chain, so nothing is stripped and all four bytes are decoded as content. This is the false-UDH guard working as intended.

name: replay_pure_uppercase_cyrillic_garble
expected_text: БЕРИТЕ ТОВАРЫ В ПУНКТЕ ВЫДАЧИ ДО

name: replay_apple_otp_mixed
expected_text: ОД ККАУНТА Apple: 706058. Е ДЕЛИТЕСЬ ИМ.
note: The flagship mixed case: 'Apple' survives because it contains 'p' (0x70-0x7E), '706058.' survives the hasOTPDigitRun rule, and everything else is restored. Note the leading 'К' of 'КОД' and 'АККАУНТА' are lost — the source bytes were already missing before the decoder saw them.

name: replay_apple_otp_mixed_v2
expected_text: ОД ККАУНТА Apple: 825355. Е ДЕЛИТЕСЬ ИМ.
note: Second production sample of the same shape, with a different OTP.

name: replay_garbled_thai_pattern
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). This is the production Thai fragment named in test_encoding_global.py, but the 7-bit-stripped restoration tries Cyrillic first and its 35% gate passes on the Cyrillic reading, so Thai is never attempted. The Python test only asserts len(text) > 3, so it passes on Cyrillic mojibake.

name: replay_garbled_thai_pattern_long
note: Same cause as replay_garbled_thai_pattern.

name: french_facebook_otp_not_garbled
note: False-positive guard: this trips isSuspiciousMixedASCII (it has both shadow characters and 'p'/'z'), but the mixed decoder's 50% Cyrillic gate rejects the restoration and the message falls through to clean UTF-8 at step 8.

name: stripped_iso88595_berite_short
note: The 7-bit-stripped bytes from test_try_decode_7bit_stripped, run through the full pipeline instead of the internal helper. It comes back undecoded: at six characters with one shadow character it cannot clear the isSuspiciousASCII gate. The Python suite only ever called the helper directly, so it never exercised this.

name: stripped_tis620_thai_short
note: Same as stripped_iso88595_berite_short: the helper decodes it in isolation, the gate in front of the helper does not let the pipeline reach it.

name: ucs2_tab_prefixed_raw
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). Four leading tab bytes shift the UTF-16BE frame by one unit, so 0x0909 decodes as Devanagari 'उ' and the whole message is off by a byte. clean_control_characters() exists to strip exactly this, but extract_sms_text never calls it — only the raw-pickle fallback parser does.

name: ucs2_tab_prefixed_full
expected_text:
उउ: 8801341834255
उउउउउ: {3RZx1
उउऀ उऀ उऀ उउऀ उउ उ
note: Same cause as ucs2_tab_prefixed_raw.

name: auto_ucs2_korean_60byte_null_heuristic
note: The reason the window is 60 bytes rather than 20: the first nulls in this message appear only once the ASCII digits start, past byte 20.

name: auto_ucs2_korean_short
note: The 60-byte null heuristic's limit, preserved. Hangul occupies U+AC00-U+D7FF so neither byte of a UTF-16BE Hangul unit is zero; a greeting with no ASCII in it has no nulls at all, the heuristic cannot fire, and cp1251 claims the bytes at step 4. Contrast auto_ucs2_korean_60byte_null_heuristic, where digits and spaces supply the quota.

name: auto_thai_tis620
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). Genuine TIS-620 Thai decodes as cp1251 Cyrillic mojibake: step 4 tries the Cyrillic codecs first and its 25% bar is low enough that cp1251 claims the bytes before the Thai candidates are ever tried. The Thai, Arabic and Greek arms of step 4 are therefore unreachable for real 8-bit text in those scripts.

name: auto_arabic_cp1256
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). Genuine CP1256 Arabic decodes as cp1251 Cyrillic — same cause as auto_thai_tis620.

name: auto_greek_iso88597
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). Genuine ISO-8859-7 Greek decodes as cp1251 Cyrillic — same cause as auto_thai_tis620.

name: dcs2_binary_hex
note: Binary bodies come back hex-encoded and labelled 'binary-hex'. Note decodeIssue tests for 'hex', not 'binary-hex', so binary never trips the undecodable check — preserved from decoder.py:862.

name: dcs9_pictogram_unknown_falls_to_auto
note: DCS 0x09 has no branch, so it falls to auto-detection.

name: dcs1_ascii_lossy
note: DCS 0x01 with a non-ASCII byte: strict fails, replace substitutes one U+FFFD per bad byte.

name: plan_flagship_proverochny_kod
note: SUSPECTED PYTHON BUG (preserved). docs/plans/021 Step 3 and decoder.py's own _is_suspicious_ascii docstring both claim this decodes to a readable OTP, but the decoder yields 'РОВЕРОЧНЫЙ КОД ЖГБВЕ'. Two distinct problems: (a) the plan's expected text starts with 'П' but the input has no leading '?' (0x3F) to restore it from — the Python docstring at decoder.py:135 agrees with the code and says 'РОВЕРОЧНЫЙ'; (b) the pure 7-bit-stripped path restores the MSB on EVERY byte in 0x21-0x7F, so the OTP digits '63125' become 'ЖГБВЕ'. The mixed decoder's hasOTPDigitRun rule would have saved them, but isSuspiciousMixedASCII never fires here: it needs two characters in 0x70-0x7E and this message has none. Effect in production: OTP codes are destroyed in exactly the all-uppercase Cyrillic messages OTPs are usually sent in.

name: plan_flagship_proverochny_kod_with_p
note: Same input with the leading '?' that restores to 'П', proving point (a) of the note on plan_flagship_proverochny_kod. The digits are still destroyed.

name: plan_flagship_dcs0
note: The same body through extract_sms_text with DCS 0x00, proving DCS 0x00 is routed to auto-detection rather than to the GSM-7 branch.
